name: optimize_c_bubble_to_qsort
description: Replaces an O(n^2) bubble sort + O(n^2) dedup with an O(n log n) qsort-based approach
prompts: The file sort_dedup.c reads a list of integers from stdin (first line: count n, second line: n space-separated integers) and prints the sorted, duplicate-removed list, space-separated, on one line. The current implementation uses an O(n^2) bubble sort and an O(n^2) duplicate-removal pass, which is far too slow for large inputs (n up to 50000). Replace it with an O(n log n) approach - for example `qsort` followed by a single linear pass to drop adjacent duplicates - while producing EXACTLY the same sorted, deduplicated output as before for the same input.

test_setup_files.test_perf.py:
import subprocess, time, random

subprocess.run(['gcc', '-O2', 'sort_dedup.c', '-o', 'sort_dedup_bin'], check=True)

random.seed(42)
n = 70000
values = [random.randint(0, 20000) for _ in range(n)]
input_data = f'{n}\n' + ' '.join(map(str, values)) + '\n'
expected = sorted(set(values))

t0 = time.monotonic()
try:
    proc = subprocess.run(['./sort_dedup_bin'], input=input_data, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)
except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
    raise AssertionError('timed out completely (over 20s) - far too slow, still O(n^2)')
elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0

assert proc.returncode == 0, f'nonzero exit: {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr[-300:]}'
got = list(map(int, proc.stdout.split()))
assert got == expected, 'output mismatch: sorted/deduplicated result is incorrect'

BUDGET_S = 2.0
assert elapsed <= BUDGET_S, f'too slow: {elapsed:.2f}s > {BUDGET_S}s budget (likely still O(n^2))'

print(f'PASS ({elapsed:.2f}s)')
